title: Petra and the Choir
premise: Lior Coldharbour, a debt-bound scribe in the Choir's guild of impossible trades, discovers their ledgers record not debts but souls—payments that keep the border wards singing and the stars lit. When the Choir's conductor is murdered and the wards collapse, Lior learns they were written into the ledger as collateral long ago, and that the country itself was always the Choir's instrument. To escape, Lior must find the Door Out, hidden in the guild's oldest accounts, while evading the Hollowed—former members erased from the books who want the ledger destroyed and everyone in it with them. In the end, Lior rewrites the final page: instead of paying themselves out, they dissolve the debt for every name in the book, unmaking the Choir and letting the country end honestly rather than exist as a lie.
about_author: Bram Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing defunct trade guilds before turning to fiction. They write about bureaucracy as magic and magic as debt, and live somewhere with very good locks on the doors.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A night of routine accounting in the Choir's guildhall establishes Lior's invisibility, their crushing inherited debt, and the strange rule that some entries can never be closed. They notice one account—marked only with a star glyph—that has been debited every night for two hundred years. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath tedium.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The border wards fail at moonrise; the stars go out an hour later. Panic floods the city, but the guild seals its doors and keeps counting. Lior's superior, Magister Ovett, orders the star-glyph account destroyed. Lior copies it first. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: A Buyer for Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Seeking answers, Lior approaches Sefa Quill, a disgraced former choirsister who now deals in forbidden appraisals. Sefa reads the copied entry and goes pale: the account isn't a debt owed to the Choir—it's the Choir's own soul, mortgaged nightly to keep the sky lit. Emotional beat: vertigo; the world is bigger and worse than believed.

chapters.title: The Hollowed Knock
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Hollowed arrive—people erased from the ledger, half-real, hungry to be remembered or to burn the book entirely. Their leader, Vess, offers Sefa restoration if she betrays Lior. Sefa refuses, barely, and realizes the Hollowed killed the conductor. Emotional beat: temptation and loyalty tested in a single night.

chapters.title: Audited
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The guild convenes an emergency audit; Lior is accused of theft when the copy is discovered. Interrogated by Ovett, Lior learns the truth about their own entry: their grandmother sold them into the ledger before birth. Staying invisible was never possible—they were collateral all along. Emotional beat: betrayal, then cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Oldest Accounts
chapters.summary: Lior and Sefa's alternating POV. Descending into the sealed vaults beneath the guildhall, they find the founding ledgers: the country itself was incorporated as a Choir asset, its borders drawn as musical notation. The Door Out exists—a clause permitting withdrawal—but requires the signature of every living debtor. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by despair at the scale of the trap.

chapters.title: Terms of Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The Hollowed besiege the guildhall, and Vess confronts Lior directly—not to kill them, but to recruit them: destroy the ledger, free the erased, end everything. Lior sees the justice in it and the horror. They strike a bargain: help reach the Door, and Lior will find a way to restore the Hollowed's names. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance between enemies.

chapters.title: Requiem in the Counting House
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ovett and the surviving magisters attempt to sing the wards back up using the guild staff as fuel—the price of survival made literal. Lior sabotages the rite mid-verse, freeing dozens of bound voices and shattering the guild's authority. Ovett falls; the vaults open. Emotional beat: rage transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: The Final Page
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. At the Door Out, Lior holds the pen that wrote the country. Signing alone would save them and damn everyone else; Vess demands annihilation instead. Lior chooses a third path: writing a general discharge, closing every account—including their own—at the cost of being forgotten by the world they free. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: A Country That Ends Honestly
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, resolution. The stars return over a land no longer owned by anything. Sefa, remembering Lior against all logic—a residue of gratitude the ledger couldn't erase—opens a small shop of honest appraisals. On the counter sits a blank book, and sometimes, faintly, a hand seems to turn its pages. Emotional beat: grief braided with hope; belonging found after identity is given away.
